# 0061: The session table scrolls sideways, and the reader picks which columns it shows

Status: accepted, 2026-10-07.
Supersedes part 3 of [0043](0043-the-overview-tables-are-budgeted-to-one-screen.md) (`SessionTable` is budgeted to one screen).
The rest of 0043 stands.

## Context

ADR 0043 budgeted `SessionTable` to one 1440px screen, taking width back from how values were spelled.
The treatment axis (ADR 0055) and the family tier (ADR 0057) each added to the row.
To stay inside the budget the treatment was capped at 7 characters, so `cheap_eval_subagents` read as `cheap_...`.
Even so, a real two-skill, two-arm capture overflowed by 128px.

Screenshots of five layouts were measured on that capture before deciding.
Trimming the identity columns, merging effort with treatment, or dropping the harness column still left 98px to 165px of overflow.
The width goes to the metric columns, and which of those matter depends on the question a reader is asking.

## Decision

**The session table scrolls sideways inside its card, with no pinned column.** The one-screen budget and its 1px smoke assertion are gone.

**A column picker sits above the table.** It is a checkbox per column, with "Select all" and "Deselect all".
`verdict` and `case` are always shown and their boxes are locked, because without them a row cannot be read.

**The choice is a per-reader preference, kept in the browser.** It is stored in `localStorage` under a versioned key, and is not part of a shared link.
Blocked storage, or a stored value of the wrong shape, falls back to showing every column.

**Width hacks that existed only for the budget are removed.** The treatment prints its full name again.

## Consequences

A new column no longer has to be paid for out of another column's width.

The smoke test now asserts the contract that replaced the budget: the box scrolls horizontally, and deselecting every optional column makes it fit any card.

A reader who hides columns sees the same table on their next visit, and a link they share opens with every column for its recipient.

## Lens

A fixed width budget makes every new column a fight over pixels, and the losing column gets truncated into noise.
Let the table be as wide as its data, and give the reader the control to make it as narrow as their question.
